facts.statement: Yanornis lived in Liaoning province, China, during the Early Cretaceous, with fossils found in the 120-million-year-old Jiufotang Formation and the 124-million-year-old Yixian Formation.
facts.quote: Two species have been described, both from Liaoning province, China: Yanornis martini, based on several fossils found in the 120-million-year-old Jiufotang Formation at Chaoyang, and Yanornis guozhangi, from the 124-million-year-old Yixian Formation.

facts.statement: The type species Yanornis martini was described based on several fossils found in the Jiufotang Formation at Chaoyang.
facts.quote: Yanornis martini, based on several fossils found in the 120-million-year-old Jiufotang Formation at Chaoyang

facts.statement: Yanornis had a well-developed U-shaped furcula, or wishbone.
facts.quote: having a well-developed U-shaped furcula (wishbone)

facts.statement: The absence of the prefrontal bone and its non-diapsid skull classify Yanornis as an ornithuromorph.
facts.quote: The absence of the prefrontal bone and the non-diapsid skull allows Yanornis to be classified as an ornithuromorph

facts.statement: The sternum of Yanornis was longer than it was wide to accommodate large flight muscles.
facts.quote: To allow for the necessarily large flight muscles, the sternum of Yanornis was longer than it was wide

facts.statement: Yanornis had feet with long toes, elongated phalanges, and relatively straight unguals.
facts.quote: The feet of yanornis had long toes, with elongated phalanges and relatively strait unguals

facts.statement: Fossil specimens preserving fish remains in the stomach and crop suggest that Yanornis was primarily a fish-eater.
facts.quote: Several fossil specimens of Y. martini preserve the remains of fish in the stomach and crop, suggesting that these birds were primarily fish-eaters

facts.statement: One specimen of Yanornis preserved large amounts of supposed gastroliths, or stomach stones, in the gizzard region.
facts.quote: One specimen preserved large amounts of supposed gastroliths ("stomach stones") in the gizzard region

facts.statement: It is debated whether Yanornis could switch its diet between fish and seeds, as later studies cast doubt on the hypothesis that the preserved stones were gastroliths used for grinding seeds.
facts.quote: This led some scientists to suggest that Yanornis was capable of "diet switching", perhaps seasonally, between fish and seeds. However, later studies cast doubt on the diet-switching hypothesis.

facts.statement: Some specimens of Yanornis have been found with long feathers on their lower limbs, giving them "four wings".
facts.quote: En algunos ejemplares se han encontrado plumas largas en las extremidades inferiores, teniendo por tanto "cuatro alas"

facts.statement: Yanornis's fish-eating diet and associated adaptations show convergent evolution with the distantly related enantiornithine Longipteryx.
facts.quote: Su alimentación de peces y las adaptaciones asociadas muestran una evolución convergente con el lejanamente emparentado enantiornitino Longipteryx

facts.statement: A 2006 study found that Yanornis, Yixianornis, and Songlingornis formed a monophyletic group.
facts.quote: In a 2006 study of early bird relationships, it was found that Yanornis, Yixianornis, and Songlingornis formed a monophyletic group

facts.statement: The order Yanornithiformes was erected to distinguish Yanornis and related birds from other early Ornithurae like Gansus.
facts.quote: The order Yanornithiformes has been erected to mark their distinctness from other early Ornithurae such as Gansus

facts.statement: Yanornis gained notoriety when its fossil was used in the paleontological forgery known as "Archaeoraptor".
facts.quote: Yanornis gained notoriety when the front half of a fossil bird was combined with the tail of a Microraptor to make the paleontological forgery "Archaeoraptor"

facts.statement: Archaeovolans repatriatus was later determined to be a junior synonym of Yanornis.
facts.quote: Archaeovolans repatriatus, which was later found to be a junior synonym of Yanornis

facts.statement: Some studies suggest that the species Aberratiodontus wui is either a poorly preserved specimen of Yanornis martini or a close relative.
facts.quote: Some studies have found that the bird species Aberratiodontus wui is in fact a poorly preserved specimen of Yanornis martini, or at least a close relative

facts.statement: Yanornis was the size of a chicken with a long skull containing about 10 teeth in the upper jaw and 20 teeth in the lower jaw.
facts.quote: Tenía el tamaño de un pollo, y tenía un cráneo largo con cerca de 10 dientes en la mandíbula superior y 20 dientes en la inferior

facts.statement: Yanornis was capable of both flying and walking well, possessing a well-developed U-shaped furcula.
facts.quote: era capaz tanto de volar como de caminar con soltura, teniendo una fúrcula en forma de U bien desarrollada

facts.statement: To accommodate large flight muscles, the sternum of Yanornis was longer than it was wide.
facts.quote: Para permitir la sujeción de los necesariamente grandes músculos de vuelo, su esternón era más largo que ancho

facts.statement: Some Yanornis specimens have long feathers on their lower limbs, resulting in "four wings".
facts.quote: En algunos ejemplares se han encontrado plumas largas en las extremidades inferiores, teniendo por tanto "cuatro alas"

facts.statement: Yanornis's fish-eating habits and related adaptations demonstrate convergent evolution with the distantly related enantiornithine Longipteryx.
facts.quote: Su alimentación de peces y las adaptaciones asociadas muestran una evolución convergente con el lejanamente emparentado enantiornitino Longipteryx

facts.statement: The genus Yanornis was named by Zhou and Zhang in 2001.

facts.statement: Yanornis belongs to the family Yanornithidae.

facts.statement: Yanornis is classified within the class Reptilia.

facts.statement: Yanornis lived during the Barremian to Aptian stages, between 125.77 and 113.2 million years ago.
